text: HCMC targets 14% industrial growth in final quarter of 2026

Ho Chi Minh City has set a target of 13.23% gross regional domestic product (GRDP) growth in the fourth quarter of 2026, with the industry and construction sector expected to expand by 14% and make a significant contribution to overall economic growth.
The city's Statistics Office reported that industrial production maintained its upward momentum in the first 10 months of the year.
The industrial production index (IIP) rose 11% year-on-year, while manufacturing and processing increased 11.4%.
In October alone, the IIP climbed 13.8%, with manufacturing and processing up 14.7%.
Several industries recorded strong growth over the 10-month period, including mechanical engineering (14.7%), food processing (11.2%) and pharmaceuticals and chemicals (10.9%).
Production across the four key industrial sectors increased 10.7%.
Electronic product manufacturing grew just 2.2%, garment production rose 3.4%, while motor vehicle manufacturing edged down 0.2%.
Under the city's fourth-quarter growth scenario, manufacturing and processing value added is targeted to increase 14.14%, requiring further acceleration in industrial output.

Analysts say the city should prioritise industries capable of quickly expanding production and fulfilling orders, while helping businesses address constraints involving working capital, raw materials, labour and logistics.
Strengthening links between major manufacturers and domestic suppliers will also be important to increase local value added and reduce reliance on imported inputs.
